thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] (an IoT company) inquires about Bluetooth registration requirements for a product built around a Silicon Labs BLE module listed on the SIG site as a Component (Tested). The consultant explains a detailed test-exemption framework (antenna choice determines RF PHY exemption, referencing the chip vendor's Component registration exempts several protocol layers, and profile testing is only required for SIG-defined standard profiles), clarifies that required registration documentation covers the whole product rather than just the module, and later identifies and resolves a set of inter-layer inconsistencies (tied to AoA/AoD and Isochronous features) that arose from combining the module's Component-level QDID with a newer Core-Spec Host/LL QDID, recommending a vendor-issued free Subset DN rather than direct ICS edits -- which Silicon Labs ultimately provided.
all_questions_found: Since the BLE module is listed on the Bluetooth SIG site as a Component (Tested), does the product need separate testing including the SoftDevice/Application software, and must that testing happen at the consultant's own facility?
Does using the module's built-in antenna versus an external antenna affect whether RF PHY testing is required?
Does referencing the chip vendor's existing Component(Tested) registration exempt the LL, L2CAP, GAP, GATT, ATT, and SM protocol layers from testing?
Does profile-layer testing depend on whether a Bluetooth SIG-defined standard profile is implemented, versus a custom profile or a profile-less implementation?

Is the customer's proposed document list (module circuit diagram, PCB layout, parts list, IC datasheet, RF test report, etc.) sufficient and limited to the Bluetooth module portion of the product, or does it need to cover the whole product?

Does Including the module's Component-level QDID together with a newer Core-Spec Host/LL QDID create inter-layer inconsistencies, and if so, how should they be resolved without triggering a large new LL-layer test requirement?
Can the QDID's Listing Owner (the chip vendor) provide a free Subset that removes the specific ICS items causing the inconsistency, and does Silicon Labs have or can they create such a Subset?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread lays out a complete test-exemption framework for a product built around a chip vendor's Component(Tested)-type BLE module: using the module's built-in antenna exempts RF PHY testing (using an external antenna would not); referencing the chip vendor's own Component(Tested) registration exempts the LL, L2CAP, GAP, GATT, ATT, and SM protocol layers from testing; and profile-layer testing is required only when implementing a Bluetooth SIG-defined standard profile, not for custom/proprietary profiles or profile-less implementations. It also covers that Bluetooth Logo certification requires documentation covering the whole product (operation manual, product block diagram, product outline drawing, antenna outline drawing, gain/radiation pattern diagram), not module-level engineering documents. Finally, it shows that combining a Component-level Controller QDID with a newer Core-Spec Host/LL QDID can produce numerous LL-RFPHY inter-layer inconsistencies tied to AoA/AoD and Isochronous features, and that the fix is to have the QDID's Listing Owner (the chip vendor) create a free Subset with the specific conflicting ICS items flipped to NO, rather than editing the LL ICS directly (which would trigger a large new LL-layer test requirement).
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Test scope for a Component(Tested)-based module product is determined by: antenna choice (built-in exempts RF PHY, external does not), whether the chip vendor's Component registration is referenced (exempts several protocol layers), and profile type (SIG-defined standard profiles require testing; custom or profile-less implementations do not). Registration documentation requirements apply to the product as a whole, not just the embedded module. When Including a Component-level QDID together with a newer Core-Spec Host/LL QDID produces inter-layer inconsistencies, the correct fix is to request a free Subset from the QDID's Listing Owner removing the specific conflicting ICS items, since directly editing the LL ICS would trigger a large new LL-layer test requirement (hundreds of items) that the Subset route avoids.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming separate testing is always required for a Component(Tested)-type module, without checking antenna configuration and chip-vendor registration references, could lead to over-quoting unnecessary tests. Submitting only module-level engineering documents instead of whole-product documentation would not satisfy the actual registration requirements. Attempting to resolve an inter-layer inconsistency by directly editing the LL ICS, rather than requesting a vendor-issued Subset, would trigger a large, costly LL-layer retest requirement that could otherwise be avoided.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When scoping a registration for a product built around a chip vendor's Component(Tested) module, walk through the test-exemption framework systematically: antenna configuration, whether the chip vendor's Component registration is referenced, and profile type, rather than assuming full testing is required. Make clear that registration documentation must cover the whole product, not just the module. When Including a Component-level QDID with a newer Core-Spec Host/LL QDID produces inter-layer inconsistencies, request a free vendor-issued Subset removing the conflicting ICS items before considering a direct ICS edit that would trigger a large new test requirement.
